Path + number → target = path, cap = number ## Orchestration ### Step 1: Gather Code **If git diff:** ```bash git diff HEAD git diff --staged ``` Combine both diffs. If both are empty, tell the user there's nothing to review. **If file/path:** Read the target file(s). If path is a directory, read all source files in it. **Always: Gather dependency context.** Look for dependency files in the project root and include them in the context sent to agents: - `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` (Node.js) - `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `Pipfile.lock` (Python) - `go.mod`, `go.sum` (Go) - `pom.xml`, `build.gradle` (Java) - `Gemfile`, `Gemfile.lock` (Ruby) - `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` (Rust) - `composer.json`, `composer.lock` (PHP) These are needed for Gilfoyle's dependency vulnerability scan. ### Step 2: Run the Debate Initialize: `round = 0`, `debate_history = []` ```dot digraph debate { "Gather code" [shape=box]; "Dispatch Gilfoyle" [shape=box]; "New issues found?" [shape=diamond]; "Dispatch Dinesh" [shape=box]; "All conceded, no pushback?" [shape=diamond]; "Round >= cap?" [shape=diamond]; "Ask user: continue?" [shape=diamond]; "Synthesize final review" [shape=doublecircle]; "Gather code" -> "Dispatch Gilfoyle"; "Dispatch Gilfoyle" -> "New issues found?"; "New issues found?" -> "Synthesize final review" [label="no — converged"]; "New issues found?" -> "Dispatch Dinesh" [label="yes"]; "Dispatch Dinesh" -> "All conceded, no pushback?"; "All conceded, no pushback?" -> "Synthesize final review" [label="yes — converged"]; "All conceded, no pushback?" -> "Round >= cap?"; "Round >= cap?" -> "Dispatch Gilfoyle" [label="no — next round"]; "Round >= cap?" -> "Ask user: continue?" [label="yes"]; "Ask user: continue?" -> "Dispatch Gilfoyle" [label="yes — extend cap"]; "Ask user: continue?" -> "Synthesize final review" [label="no"]; } ``` **Each round:** 1. **Dispatch Gilfoyle agent** (Agent tool, general-purpose) with: - Full content of `gilfoyle-agent.md` from this skill's directory - The code under review - Full debate history - Round number - Instruction: "You are doing research only — read the code and produce your review. If all findings are repeats from previous rounds → converge. 4. **Dispatch Dinesh agent** (Agent tool, general-purpose) with: - Full content of `dinesh-agent.md` from this skill's directory - The code under review - Gilfoyle's latest full response - Full debate history - Round number - Instruction: "You are doing research only — read the code and produce your defense. Do NOT edit any files." 5. **Display Dinesh's banter** to the user. 6. **Check convergence:** Parse Dinesh's FINDINGS section. If every point is `[concede]` with zero `[defend]` or `[dismiss]` → converge. 7. **Append both responses to debate_history**, increment round. 8. **If round >= cap:** Ask user: *"These two could go all night. Continue for more rounds? (y/N)"* - Yes → extend cap by original amount, continue loop - No → proceed to synthesis **Convergence announcements** (pick one that fits): - "Gilfoyle has run out of things to hate. Unprecedented." - "Dinesh has conceded defeat. As expected." - "These two are going in circles. Separating them before it gets physical." ### Step 3: Synthesize Final Review After the debate ends, produce a structured summary from the full debate transcript. **Display format:** ```markdown ## Dinesh vs Gilfoyle Review — [target] ### [N] rounds of mass destruction --- ### Best of the Banter [2-4 of the funniest or most insightful exchanges from the debate] --- ### Verdict #### Critical (Gilfoyle won, Dinesh conceded) [Issues where Dinesh couldn't mount a defense — these are real and need fixing] - `file:line` — issue — fix #### Important (Gilfoyle won after debate) [Issues Dinesh tried to defend but Gilfoyle's argument was stronger] - `file:line` — issue — fix #### Contested (Dinesh held his ground) [Issues where Dinesh's defense was valid — code is likely fine] - `file:line` — what was raised — why the defense holds #### Dismissed (Gilfoyle was nitpicking) [Issues both sides agree don't matter] - `file:line` — what was raised — why it's a non-issue ### Strengths [Things even Gilfoyle grudgingly acknowledged were good] ### Score Gilfoyle: X | Dinesh: Y [Tongue-in-cheek tally of who won more arguments] ### Recommended Changes [Clean checklist — no banter, no context, just what to do] - [ ] `file:line` — what to change - [ ] `file:line` — what to change - [ ] ... If no changes needed: "Nothing to fix. Gilfoyle is furious." ``` ### Step 4: Offer Comic Strip After displaying the final review, ask the user: > *"Want a comic strip of the best moments? Write the filled HTML to a timestamped file: `/tmp/dg-comic-{timestamp}.html` **If `y`:** 5. Open it in the browser: `open /tmp/dg-comic-{timestamp}.html` 6. Tell the user where the file is saved. **If `pr`:** 5. Convert to PNG using a headless browser: ```bash # Try puppeteer/chromium first, fall back to wkhtmltoimage, then to Safari npx --yes puppeteer-screenshot /tmp/dg-comic-{timestamp}.html /tmp/dg-comic-{timestamp}.png 2>/dev/null \ || wkhtmltoimage --quality 90 /tmp/dg-comic-{timestamp}.html /tmp/dg-comic-{timestamp}.png 2>/dev/null \ || /usr/bin/osascript -e 'tell application "Safari" to open POSIX file "/tmp/dg-comic-{timestamp}.html"' ``` If screenshot tools aren't available, tell the user to screenshot manually from the browser. 6. ```rust

```rust
if words.next().is_some() { return false; }
```

More than one word? Return false. But you only *called* it when there are three or more words. So it returns `false`. Every time. Forever. The `http://`, the `https://`, the `ftp://`, the semver detector you were so proud of — a monument to nothing. It is architecturally impossible for that function to ever return `true`. You wrote a lock, tested the lock, and installed it on a wall.

Also dead. The *only* branch that ever fires is `is_all_caps`, which means your entire "is this an identifier" heuristic has collapsed into "is this shouting." Congratulations, you skip `THIS IS SPARTA` and lint everything else. All that code, and the effective logic is `word_count >= 3 && !all_caps`. You could have deleted 150 lines and shipped the same behavior. Your unit tests pass because they call the corpses directly, one word at a time. In the actual pipeline they never get a heartbeat.

Now `lib.rs`. `create_mask` builds a `TreeSitterMasker` for comments, parses the entire document, then builds a *second* `TreeSitterMasker` for scalars and parses **the entire document again.** Two full tree-sitter parses of the same source to walk the same tree twice. One parse, one walk, two predicates. You knew that. You just liked typing `.create_mask(source)` twice.

`is_scalar_node` → `is_mapping_key` decides a scalar is a key by comparing `start_byte()` to the pair's `start_byte()`. Cute, works for `key: value`. Now feed it an explicit key:

```yaml
? some long key
: the value
```

The pair starts at `?`, the key scalar starts two bytes later, `start != start`, so your code decides the *key* is a *value* and cheerfully grammar-checks it. Edge case, sure. Your fuzz target feeds arbitrary bytes, so it's an edge case that will visit you.

Block scalars: you mask the whole `block_scalar` node, which includes the `|` or `>` indicator. `split_whitespace` counts `|` as a word, so a two-word block scalar becomes "three words, must be prose," and then `PlainEnglish` gets to lint a pipe character. Elegant.

The one thing that isn't broken: `dedent.rs`. The `trim` underflow I went looking for isn't there — the `?` on the leading `position` guarantees a trailing non-whitespace char exists, so `len - rev_position` can't wrap. I checked it three times because I refused to believe you'd gotten arithmetic right. You did. Don't let it go to your head.

Done, Rod. Single commit `68ae54b5` pushed to `feature/yaml-support-design` on your fork.

## What the two sonnet subagents fixed

| Fix | File | What changed |
|-----|------|--------------|
| **Dead code removal** | `heuristics.rs` | Deleted `looks_url_path_or_version`, `is_semver_like`, `is_snake_or_kebab_case`; simplified `looks_like_identifier` to the all-caps check. **Behaviour-preserving** — the `word_count >= 3` gate already subsumed every case those helpers claimed to handle. |
| **Block-scalar indicators** | `heuristics.rs` | New `strip_block_scalar_indicator` removes a leading `\|`/`>` header (and chomping/indent variants like `\|-`, `>+2`) before word-counting, so a short body isn't shoved over the prose threshold by the indicator. Guarded so mid-sentence pipes aren't touched. |
| **`is_mapping_key`** | `lib.rs` | Byte-position heuristic → tree-sitter's named `key` field, so explicit-key syntax (`? key` / `: value`) no longer mislints the key. |
| **Overlap guard** | `lib.rs` | Coalesces overlapping spans before the `Mask` collect, closing the `FromIterator` panic (a DoS vector in harper-ls) on adversarial input. |

Verification: `cargo test -p harper-yaml` → **47 tests green** (44 unit + 3 file-based), `harper-ls`/`harper-cli` still build, `cargo fmt --check` clean.

## Two findings I did *not* act on
- **Double tree-sitter parse** — you chose to skip it. The two-masker design is load-bearing (separate whitespace-merge domains), and the clean fix would have meant touching the shared `harper-tree-sitter` crate — against Harper's "keep PRs brief" policy.
- **`.yml` routing gap** — turned out **not to be a real bug**. `harper-ls` dispatches by LSP language ID (`"yaml"`, which editors assign to both `.yaml` and `.yml`), and `harper-cli` already matches both extensions. Nothing to fix.

Two notes for when this branch becomes an upstream PR: Harper's `AGENT_POLICY.md` asks for (1) an LLM-authorship disclaimer in the PR description, and (2) ideally splitting into small PRs — this crate is already sizeable, so you may want the YAML feature and these fixes as separate reviewable units. The `just format` JS/prettier step is also failing independently of this work (`paths were provided but ignored: .`) — worth a look, but I left it alone since it's unrelated.
